rv.q: The National’s magnificent production of Caryl Churchill’s English civil war play resonates powerfully today.
I’d recommend the production to anyone who doesn’t know the play, while still feeling that it works best when presented with a minimalist austerity that matches Churchill’s text.
It's easy to see why Norris chose this and to appreciate the gesture being made here, but stirring as it is at times, it feels like a pretty whisper rather than a roar.
However, it is also a flinty play with little humour and scant theatricality; a case of ‘Give me metaphor or give me death.’
The first production programmed by Norris, and presumably conceived and executed with his specific blessing, is a triumph of form over substance.
By the end, I envied Charles I the loss of his head.

cn.t: Critics are divided on Lyndsey Turner's revival of Churchill's 1976 classic — the epic 62-person staging impresses with stunning design but risks overwhelming the text.
